verses.1: Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?
verses.2: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed, saying ,
verses.3: Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.
verses.4: He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the LORD shall have them in derision.
verses.5: Then shall he speak to them in his wrath, and trouble them in his sore displeasure.
verses.6: Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion.
verses.7: I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said to me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.
verses.8: Ask of me, and I will give thee the heathen for thy inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.
verses.9: Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.
verses.10: Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.
verses.11: Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
verses.12: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.

metadata.source: Derived from Webster's Bible (1833), revised as a poetic KJV-tradition translation filtered through the theology of abiding in Christ.
